slides.title: About this build
slides.lead: An enclosure prototype for learning, fitting and improving
body: This guide walks through an unpowered mechanical build using the measured display and protected battery-holder envelopes.
The top cartridge contains the gas sensors. The battery and future main PCB sit behind the screen.
Keep a fit log as you work. Measurements from your actual parts matter more than their appearance in CAD.

rows: Native CAD and actual Fusion views
Real seals, wire bends and connectors

slides.note: Unpowered fit first. Fastening needs qualified insert coupons and updated pilots. Native Fusion is authoritative. STEP retains a numerical volume exception; see EXPORT_NOTES.md.

slides.title: Exterior and orientation
slides.lead: {{case_h}} high x {{case_w}} wide x {{case_d}} deep, in millimetres
body: Screen at the front, one cover at the rear, button on the left and USB-C below. Upper side fittings connect the sample.
Drawing coordinates: +X toward your left, +Y up and +Z rearward.
slides.note: Left and right refer to facing the screen. The bottom view is rotated on the page. Gas-fitting references extend beyond the main body.

slides.title: Assembly overview
slides.lead: The rear cover keeps the removable assemblies in place
body: P01 housing supports the display retainers, holder cradle and electronics carrier.
P07 manifold and P08 lid form an independent cartridge. Its external fittings and harness disconnect before removal.
P06, P09 and P10 form the bottom USB cartridge.
The exploded view shows part ownership. Follow the service sequence on page 19 for actual removal.
slides.note: Short labels P01-P11 expand to TMX-A3-P01 through TMX-A3-P11 in the BOM and mesh manifest.

slides.note: Use the matching release meshes and print manifest. The older CAD names for P09 and P10 contain the word metal because they preserve the original design history.

slides.title: Printing the fit prototype
slides.lead: Bambu H2D preparation
body: The starting process uses four walls, five top/bottom layers, 20% gyroid infill and a 4 mm outer brim.
Review the prepared supports and gas-passage blockers. Keep sealing faces clean and remove all loose material.
Use the PLA project for dimensional fit. PETG is the target for the later enclosure trial, including the USB interfaces and AO2 adapter.

rows: Use the orientations in the print manifest
Inspect the recorded per-part support strategy
Print the insert and mating-fit coupons first

slides.note: Inspect the two recorded P07 layer transitions after printing. The profile remains a starting point; record filament and any changes.

slides.title: Tools and measurements
slides.lead: A few measurements prevent most assembly surprises
body: Prepare calipers, the correct hex drivers, an insert installation tool, deburring tools and a clean padded work surface.
Begin with no power connected. Use the empty holder or nonconductive fit references while checking the printed enclosure.

rows: Display frame lip and cable exits
Retainer contact surfaces and free cable route
Panel fit, insertion depth and release access
Exposed sensing faces, seals and clear passage

slides.note: Record measured values in the fit checklist. The cells and small connector details in CAD remain dimensional references.

slides.title: Heat-set inserts
slides.lead: The insert coupon comes before the full enclosure
body: Remove support and loose material, then trial-fit the printed parts. Preserve sealing lands and alignment edges.
An insert gives the printed boss a metal thread. Its exact outer profile determines the required printed pilot hole.
Select the insert SKU, print its coupon and use the manufacturer's installation method. Check cooled retention and screw engagement.
Revise the enclosure pilot holes to the qualified result before heat installation in full parts. Until then, continue the loose dimensional fit.
A screw that bottoms out can feel tight before it clamps. Check its length and the joint after the coupon succeeds.
slides.note: Existing M2 holes around 3.2/3.3 mm and M3 holes around 4.3 mm are generic clearance references. They are not approved heat-set retention pilots.

slides.title: Step 1: Display and retainers
slides.lead: The factory casing remains around the screen
body: Keep the factory back panel removed, as in the measured configuration. Protect the glass on a clean padded surface.
Fit the complete cased display into its front opening. Route its cables through the intended clear space.
Install the lower P04 and upper P05 retainers from the rear with their two M2 screws.
The retainers should capture the frame evenly. Check for display movement, frame distortion and pressure on the glass.
slides.note: Frame lip, contact area and preload remain physical checks. During service, remove the retainers rearward and the complete display forward.

slides.title: Step 2: Bottom USB cartridge
slides.lead: The connector load passes into a removable support
body: P09 forms the small external bezel. P06 supports the connector and the 0.60 mm daughterboard.
P10 captures the assembly with two rear-accessible M2 screws. Align it without using the screws to force the parts together.
The printed bezel keeps a local 1.80 mm connector seat. Check plug insertion with the actual cable, then inspect the PCB and solder tabs for movement.
Fit the complete cartridge at the bottom opening and keep its VBUS/GND loom accessible for disconnection.
slides.note: PETG is the target material. PLA serves the fit trial. P09 keeps a local 1.80 mm seat exception and the GCT gasket remains uncompressed in CAD. Test seal and load behavior physically.

slides.title: Step 3: Button and carrier
slides.lead: A clear service route protects the future wiring
body: Fit the left momentary button with its supplied panel hardware. Confirm terminal clearance before attaching any loom.
Install P03 using the two shared carrier/PCB positions. A dummy board can verify the mechanical allocation.
Check both PCB notches against the button intrusion and the USB service route.
Keep connector access and screw heads visible. Plan wire slack so the carrier can move without pulling solder joints.
slides.note: The notched main-PCB envelope is a mechanical allocation. A routed KiCad board and final harness drawing remain separate deliverables.

slides.title: Step 4: Protected battery holder
slides.lead: The pack remains removable without dismantling the carrier
body: Trial-fit the measured FMA holder in its cradle. Check its protection-board protrusions and wire exit against the print.
Place the battery disconnect where its latch or grip can be reached after removing the cover.
Confirm that the holder withdraws rearward with the carrier and chamber in place.
Use the protected holder leads in the eventual electrical assembly. Cell identity, polarity, protection and charge limits require the electrical commissioning process.
slides.note: The owner confirmed two 3400 mAh cells. The mechanical model does not verify their manufacturer, chemistry limits or actual dimensions.

slides.title: Step 5: Sampling cartridge
slides.lead: The sensing passage stays separate from the electronics
body: P07 carries the inlet passage, sensor regions and return channel. P08 closes it with four screws.
The AO2 body stays on the dry side. Its threaded nose faces the sample through P11.
The BME280 provision sits upstream and apart from the MD62 body.
Housing guides locate the closed cartridge. The rear cover captures it without extra cartridge-to-housing screws.
slides.note: The 5 mm digital probe checks geometric passage only. Leakage, sample renewal, humidity and thermal response require physical tests.

slides.title: Step 6: Sensor placement
slides.lead: Sensing faces and leads need clear, gentle support
body: Fit the purchased modules against their reference seats before connecting wires. Confirm that each contact surface is safe for that sensor.
Keep the AO2 membrane and CO sensing face clear. Keep sealant and loose print debris away from all sensing surfaces.
Retain the MD62 lead allowance until its actual pitch, detector marking and support method are confirmed.
Provide insulation and strain relief for each lead or harness. Check the humidity board's true outline and BME280 identity.
slides.note: MD62 is upper left, BME280 upper right, CO lower left and AO2 lower right. MD62 helium use remains experimental. Sensor lead and surface details are illustrative.

slides.title: Step 7: Lid, adapter and seals
slides.lead: Seal selection completes the chamber interface
body: Inspect the P07/P08 mating lands and the internal divider contacts before selecting seal stock.
P11 has a modeled M16 x 1 female thread. Trial-fit the purchased AO2 nose by hand and check engagement, the stop and sealing datum.
Choose a compatible face seal and harness closure. Record material, dimensions and assembly method.
Close the lid evenly on the bench. Its four screws apply the chamber clamping force independently of the outer cover.
slides.note: Thread fit, seal compression, hand-tight AO2 sealing and leak performance remain physical gates. The printed enclosure is not a pressure-regulating device.

slides.title: Step 8: Rear cover
slides.lead: The cover closes without pressing on wires or components
body: Seat the cartridge and the other assemblies, then route the unpowered harness references.
Check the battery disconnect, button terminals and USB loom for free access.
Guide the cover tabs into their locating interface by hand. The small lead-ins help alignment. Seat the cover fully before fitting screws.
Fit the four rear screws gradually. Reopen the cover and inspect for rub marks, trapped wires or parts that shifted.
slides.note: Record wire clearance and contact marks in the fit checklist, then verify that each connector can still be released.

slides.title: Service sequence
slides.lead: The same rear opening supports each routine removal

rows: Harness free, both gas fittings removed
Cover and battery out, USB loom free

slides.note: Open the chamber and USB cartridge on the bench. Keep their own screws with them during enclosure withdrawal. Verify every route with your actual wiring.

slides.title: Fit record and next release
slides.lead: A useful prototype leaves a clear set of measurements
body: Photograph the exact fit issue and include its stable part ID. Change one parameter at a time and rerun the affected checks.
A successful fit prototype closes dimensional questions. Record sealing and electrical results separately.

rows: Measured value, location and printer settings
Selected SKU, installation and joint result
Wire clearance, grip and tools used

slides.note: The companion checklist provides space for measurements and pass/pending results.

slides.title: Electrical and measurement handoff
slides.lead: Mechanical fit is one stage of the complete instrument
body: Reconcile the A3 PCB outline and connector positions with electrical A2.2. Complete placement, routing, thermal copper and DRC before fabrication.
Qualify the charging circuit, protected pack, temperature sensing and Guition power isolation. Test both USB cable arrangements using the electrical test record.
Implement the real sensor and battery drivers, power-off sequence and fault handling. The present application still supports simulated readings.
Validate gas flow, seals, calibration and response before treating readings as measurements.
slides.note: This package supports an enclosure fit prototype. Complete-device assembly and gas-analysis qualification remain open work.

slides.lead: A clear source trail helps the next builder
body: Project: github.com/magnus188/aegir
Project-created CAD and print files: CERN-OHL-S-2.0. Project-written scripts: GPL-3.0-only. See License details.
Manufacturer references: Honeywell AO2, Winsen MD62 and ZE07-CO, Bosch BME280, and GCT USB4720. The models are drawing-derived references.
Contribute measured dimensions, print settings and test results with the part ID and release identifier. Include a clear photo and an editable change when possible.
